title: Escape: One Day We Had to Run...
author: Ming and Wah Chen
target_audience: Families discussing history and human rights
Readers interested in refugee stories and perseverance
core_themes: Courage in the face of danger
Historical and contemporary escapes from oppression
primary_purpose: To introduce younger readers to real-life stories of individuals and families who have had to flee their homes due to persecution or conflict, highlighting the bravery, resourcefulness, and hopefulness of refugees across different cultures and time periods.

structure_format.narrative_style: Accessible and empathetic, merging narrative nonfiction with poetic language
structure_format.organization: Each spread presents a distinct story of escape, often featuring brief, impactful text alongside vivid illustrations
features: Stories from a global, historical perspective
Accompanying factual blurbs for each escape

key_concepts_lessons: Escaping danger is a reality faced by diverse people across the globe and throughout history.
Acts of bravery and ingenuity define many refugee journeys.
Understanding personal stories fosters empathy and awareness of the refugee experience.
Historic and contemporary escapes share common threads of hope and determination.
Children can learn the importance of human rights and justice through real accounts.
notable_features: Globally diverse range of escape stories—including from Nazi Germany, the Vietnam War, and contemporary Syria
Short, poetic and fact-based storytelling suitable for middle grade readers
Emphasizes real-life heroes who used ingenuity and courage to escape adversity
cultural_historical_context: Published in the early 2020s amidst heightened public discourse around refugees, migration, and human rights, the book spotlights both historic and ongoing struggles for freedom, aiming to cultivate empathy in young readers.
reception_impact: Praised by teachers and librarians for bringing tough topics to a younger audience in an age-appropriate, sensitive way
Recommended for classroom discussions on refugees and human rights
Appreciated for its global perspective and hopeful message despite difficult subject matter
Some reviewers note the text’s brevity invites valuable discussion and further research
comparable_titles: Stepping Stones: A Refugee Family’s Journey by Margriet Ruurs
